newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to shut all but one local plants after fire.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to shut all but one local plants after fire.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp will halt vehicle production on Tuesday at all of its domestic plants except one, at Daihatsu Motor Co Ltd, due to a fire at a key parts supplier, a Toyota spokesman told Reuters on Monday.
Toyota cars are produced at 12 plants, including at Daihatsu and Toyota's affiliates.
The fire on Saturday at an Aisin Seiki Co Ltd plant halted output of brake parts supplied to Toyota.

An Aisin spokesman said earlier that the firm would be unable to supply some brake-related products to Toyota as it had not found an alternative production facility. About 90 percent of the company's products are shipped to Toyota.
"We will decide on Tuesday afternoon the production schedule for Wednesday," the Toyota spokesman said.
Toyota will make efforts to resume a normal level of production by the beginning of next week, the spokesman said.
Toyota has not disclosed how many vehicles it was unable to produce on Monday.
Toyota produces cars and trucks at 30 domestic production lines including its affiliates such as Daihatsu, with a daily output rate of 14,000 vehicles.
Of the total 30 lines, only eight were operating on Monday due to lack of brake components.

Ten Toyota affiliates such as Denso Co Ltd, Toyoda Machine Works Ltd, and Toyoda Automatic Loom Works Ltd will start producing brake master cylinders and proportioning valves in place of Aisin in the near future, the spokesman said.
The parts are used in most models of Toyota vehicles. A proportioning valve is part of the brake system to provide equal pressure to brake pistons at all wheels.
